subject: SLO constraints & context-token impact — follow-up from demo
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acme-ai.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: SLO constraints & context-token impact — follow-up from demo

Samira — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned as you evaluate Redwood for the Acme conversational assistant: 

Key constraints you shared (TL;DR):
- Latency target: p95 <= 300ms for short queries (<= 512 tokens total) and p95 <= 800ms for longer interactions (up to 8k tokens).
- Concurrency: sustained 200 concurrent sessions during business hours, ability to burst to ~500 for promotional spikes.
- Streaming: important for partial-turn streaming to UX (progressive responses), with server-sent events acceptable.
- Context window: mixed; core flows use ~1.5k input tokens + 512 output tokens, but escalation flows push to ~6k input + 1k output occasionally.

Notes on likely impact:
- Long context (>=6k) will materially increase tokenization and KV cache memory, adding ~150–300ms per request at current quantized settings on A100-class hosts.
- Streaming reduces perceived latency but requires keeping the attention/kvcache warm — this can be accomplished with our streaming-optimized pipelines, but costs scale with active concurrent streams.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) We’ll run a short performance sweep using your sample workload (you agreed to share a trimmed logs CSV).
2) Rishi will draft an SLO proposal showing cost/latency tradeoffs for 3 operating modes (low-cost batch, balanced, low-latency streaming).
3) Marissa will coordinate procurement steps and confirm required SOC evidence for Private deployment if needed.

Attachments: I attached the demo logs you dropped in the call and a draft SLO proposal (v1) to get the conversation started.

Can you confirm the traffic split between short-turn queries and the escalation flows (estimate in %)? If you can send that by EOD Wednesday we’ll prioritize the perf sweep.

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov | Senior AE, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

On Mon, May 18, 2026 at 09:30 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Samira — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned as you evaluate Redwood for the Acme conversational assistant:

Thanks Olga — that captures it well. A couple clarifications: 
- Traffic split: ~78% short-turn (<=512 tokens), ~18% mid (512–3k), ~4% escalation (3k–8k). Escalation occurs for ~2% of users but is critical for compliance summaries.
- Streams: prefer server-sent events; mobile clients will drop and re-connect sometimes — how will that affect memory on your side?
- Peak burst: our marketing spikes last ~30–45 minutes, we need the platform to scale predictably for those bursts.

We’ll upload the anonymized logs by EOD — attaching a small sample in the thread. Also looping in procurement for any questions on POs and standard terms.

Regards,
Samira Khan
Head of Product, Acme AI
samira.khan@acme-ai.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SLO constraints & context-token impact — follow-up from demo

Fwding Samira’s clarifications. Quick internal notes for the perf sweep and proposal: 

- Rishi: prioritize a run that mirrors the 78/18/4 split Samira provided. For escalation flows, test both a) 6k context with 1k output and b) truncated context (keep last 1k tokens) to show degradation vs cost. Capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
- Measure streaming memory footprint per concurrent stream; simulate mobile reconnections (SSE reconnect) at a 5% reconnection rate per minute to estimate KV cache churn.
- Marissa: flag procurement for a potential Dedicated pilot (1–2 nodes reserved) and request SOC 2 evidence set in parallel.

I’ll draft the email to Samira with the proposed timeline: perf-sweep results by Fri, a conflated SLO/cost tradeoff doc Monday next week, and a small canary plan for a low-latency streaming mode.

—Olga

(On internal note: attach run-template.csv to perf job — created in /shared/perf-templates)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Samira — thanks for the quick reply and the sample. Confirming next steps and timeline: 

Planned deliverables & schedule:
- Today (EOD): we received your sample (confirmed).
- Wed 20 May: perf sweep start — we’ll run the 78/18/4 traffic mix. Expect a short report with p50/p95/p99 and token-cost breakdown.
- Fri 22 May: consolidated perf sweep results + proposed SLO tiers ("balanced", "low-latency", "cost-optimized") with cost delta estimates.
- Week of May 25: optional 48-hour canary on a dedicated pool to validate streaming behavior under reconnections (if you greenlight).

Decisions we need from you to prioritize:
1) Will you accept a canary on a Dedicated reserved pool (we’ll size for 200 sustained + 500 burst)? Reply Yes/No.
2) Are you willing to tolerate truncated context for the lowest-cost tier (we’ll show both quality and latency tradeoffs)? Yes/No.

Logistics & PO/procurement: I’ve CC’d Marissa to start the paperwork. For SOC 2, we can share our SOC report and mapping doc once we have a signed NDA/loi.

I’ll attach the initial perf template and the SLO proposal (v1) in case your team wants to annotate before Friday.

Best,
Olga
